target_customer: Hospitals, rural health systems, DME companies and billing teams that lose revenue to denied insurance claims
problem: Providers lose large sums to denied claims and lack staff to appeal them one by one.
business_model: Success-based fee on recovered revenue (no subscription per company site)
product_category: AI denial management and appeals for healthcare

founders.name: Krishang Todi
prior_employers: Fixed-income risk modeling at an Indian fund (name not given)
education: Carnegie Mellon, economics and computational finance

founders.name: Dhanya Shah
education: Carnegie Mellon (per YC launch post, all three founders are CMU alumni)
founders.background_notes: Full-stack engineer who built production systems at three companies per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Drafting appeals with LLMs is easy; integrating with Epic and other EHRs, clearinghouses and payer portals and applying payer policy logic is the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and outcome data help, but many startups and legacy RCM vendors sell similar appeal automation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from opened sources; later press shows funded AI denial startups such as Adonis and Amperos.

market_need_then: Denied claims are a recognized multi-billion dollar problem; the founders began after a personal denied-claim experience (YC launch account) and the company claims a 78 percent overturn rate and large time savings, unverified.

branding.domain_note: Uses aegishealth.us (not the .com), suggesting aegis.com was unavailable; no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and outcome focused: AI that uplifts revenue from denied claims

branding.community_and_virality: Two Forbes Tech Council founder articles (Aug 2025) and a Business Insider mention among top AI agent startups at YC Demo Day, per company site.

brand_strength.rationale: Aegis means shield, a common and confusable name shared with unrelated companies; thought leadership helped awareness a little.

outcome_analysis: Aegis is a three person Spring 2025 company selling AI denial appeals on a success fee to hospitals and DME companies. It lists YC, Rebel Fund and Sequoia Scout among investors and claims strong overturn rates, but no round size is verified. It is early, active and unexited, in a segment where better funded AI revenue cycle startups emerged in 2026.
notes: Round recorded without an amount because only the company site names investors. PitchBook reportedly lists 500K raised with a different investor set (adds The Impact Venture, omits Sequoia Scout and Maiora); single aggregator, unverified. YC page text on Dhanya Shah's education was hedged. Competitors named in search (Adonis, Thoughtful AI, Amperos) are 2026 sources, so the dated list is empty. Confidence low because funding amount and competition could not be dated.
